messages.author: 12eeef275b63e690
messages.subject: Added growth LGM
parts:
Dear Lavaan users,

I am trying to find out if it is possible to implement a multigroup added growth LGM, such as the one one in the path diagram below (figure 4; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2888524/). In the study that I am proposing, we are anticipating that one group will follow a linear trend and the other will follow a quadratic trend. I assume that this model may be able to address that question? I have seen that lavaan can fit multigroup LGM but was unsure if it is possible to specify a different structure in each group? 

Thanks for you help.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Added growth LGM
parts: I have seen that lavaan can fit multigroup LGM but was unsure if it is possible to specify a different structure in each group?

You can specify different structures per group using block-structured syntax:

https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/uyq3h0wXh6g/m/wne8Z83wAwAJ

Or you can simply set the loadings for the added-growth factor to zero in the group posited to have only linear growth.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Added growth LGM
parts: is this the correct way to fix the loadings in group 2 to zero for the quadratic part?
If you are defining separate blocks per group, you don't need to specify the quadratic slope at all (that is the advantage of the blocked syntax).

model <- ' 
group: 1
  i  =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4

s  =~        1*t2 + 2*t3 + 3*t4
  s2 =~        1*t2 + 4*t3 + 9*t4

group: 2
  i =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4

s =~        1*t2 + 2*t3 + 3*t4
'

Setting them to zero would be necessary if you just used a standard syntax for multigroup models, with a vector of parameters.
 
model <- ' 
  i  =~ c(1,1)*t1 +   c(1,1)*t2 + c(1,1)*t3 + c(1,1)*t4 
  s  =~               c(1,1)*t2 + c(2,2)*t3 + c(3,3)*t4
  s2 =~               c(1,0)*t2 + c(4,0)*t3 + c(9,0)*t4 
  s2 ~~ c(NA, 1)*s2
  s2 ~ c(NA, 0)*1
'

In the second case, you would also need to fix the latent mean/variance in Group 2 (in bold above) because they cannot be estimated.
Also, can this model then be used to check invariance between the groups? Our main focus is to determine if the two groups have different trajectory shapes.

If you want to test whether the quadratic slope is null in the second group, then compare one of the restricted models above to a model in which the quadratic effect is estimated in both groups, then use lavTestLRT() to compare the models.  If you only have a quadratic effect specified in a single group, then your model already says the trajectories differ; there is no test, it is the assumption of your model specification.
